questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check the front of the trailer for damage. Look for cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on lane usage. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, stay in the correct lane. Do not cross curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. When multiple lanes exist, use the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use the four-way flashers because this is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, all of the following should be true, except:

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: When checking air and electrical lines, listen for leaks. The lines should not be cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging against parts.

questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:
questions.explanation: During a bus evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct all students to use it.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each item. Explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or hood.

questions.question: During a bus evacuation, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.
questions.explanation: Lead students at least 100 feet from the road in the direction of oncoming traffic. This protects them from debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: A blind spot behind a school bus extends at least ____ feet.
questions.explanation: School buses have blind spots below and in front of the side mirrors and directly behind the rear bumper. Rear blind spots typically extend 50 to 150 feet behind the bus.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, pull past the alley and position your vehicle parallel to the outer boundary. Back the vehicle into the parking area. Park it straight within the boundaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a properly charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What can a driver see using outside crossover mirrors?

options.text: The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see the danger zone in front of the bus. They also show the danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight ahead and do not let the vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the on-road test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: Check traffic in all directions. Reduce your speed before the curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Keep your vehicle in its lane and continue checking traffic.

questions.question: After passing under an overpass during the driving skills test, you may be asked to recall:

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the roadway.

questions.explanation: The examiner may ask you to recall the posted clearance or height of an overpass you drove under during the test.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers when approaching and crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off once your entire vehicle has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, they should:

options.text: Hurry and pick up the item.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could step into the driver's blind spot. Instead, students should move away from the danger zone, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: Loading a school bus:
questions.explanation: More students die during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow proper safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: Which backing maneuver will you NOT be asked to perform during the basic control skills test?
questions.explanation: The basic control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
May turn to face the road before completely exiting.
Must be facing away from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Drive safely during the test. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals, follow all traffic laws, and avoid accidents and moving violations.
